page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Esv6 server family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2090.0 and strong text processing capabilities. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 3972.36 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4757.0. Memory bandwidth is also a notable bottleneck, with uncached read and write speeds falling into the bottom 25% tier at 35.14 GB/sec and 24.76 GB/sec respectively. Despite these memory bandwidth constraints, the instance maintains average performance in database operations, static web serving, and single-threaded compression tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4s_v6 offers high memory density per active vCPU, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. This resource profile is well-suited for relational database hosting, caching layers, enterprise application servers, and memory-intensive text processing pipelines.
